steps.caption: System Console → Plugins → Plugin Management: upload the bridge bundle and enable it.
The bridge settings: homeserver URL and the two appservice tokens the plugin generated.
Further down, the registration file for the homeserver is generated from these settings.
`/matrix test` confirms the homeserver connection and the appservice permissions.
For a channel that existed before the bridge, `/matrix create publish=true` creates a public Matrix room and bridges it.
A channel created after the bridge was enabled gets a room automatically; `/matrix status` shows it.
In Element, a Matrix user opens the bridged room: the bridge bot created it, so it is a normal Matrix room.
After joining, the member list shows the bridge bot and a ghost user for every channel member.
Back in Mattermost, the Matrix user appears as a remote user who joined the channel.
Ada posts a formatted message in Mattermost.
The same message in Element, sent by Ada's ghost user with her name and avatar, formatting intact.
Alice's reply arrives in Mattermost as a remote user with her Matrix display name and avatar.
A Mattermost thread with a reply from Carol and one from Alice on Matrix.
In Element the same conversation is a Matrix thread under Ada's message.
Ada edits her post; Element shows the edited message with the "(edited)" marker.
Alice edits her Matrix message; Mattermost updates the post and marks it "Edited".
Reactions from both networks on one post: Carol's 🎉 from Mattermost and Alice's 👍 from Matrix.
The same reactions in Element.
Alice mentions Carol's ghost in Element; Mattermost renders it as an @carol mention.
Ada mentions Alice's remote account in Mattermost; Element shows a pill for Alice.
An image attached in Mattermost arrives in Element as an m.image event.
An image sent from Element shows up as a file attachment in Mattermost.
Typing in Element shows a typing indicator in Mattermost (appservice ephemeral events).
Alice changes the room topic in Matrix; the Mattermost channel header follows.
The room in Element with the new topic.
Dave is added to the channel and Bob joins from Matrix: both show up on both sides.
Element's member list: the bridge bot, Matrix users, and a ghost for each Mattermost member.
`/matrix link` gives Carol a one-time code for the bridge bot in Matrix.
In Element, the bridge bot confirms the link and, after `!mattermost login`, double puppeting.
Carol's Mattermost message in Element, sent by her linked Matrix account rather than a ghost.
Carol starts a Mattermost call; Element shows who started it, with a link to join. Audio and video stay in Mattermost.
A call started from Matrix shows in the channel as a card with a join button.
`/matrix call` starts a call both sides can join through Element Call.
The same call in Element: an announcement with the join link, and a widget in the room.
The bridge panel, opened from the Matrix icon in the app bar: the room this channel is bridged to, who is in it, a button to start a call, and how you appear in Matrix.
Linking an account from the panel shows the code to send to the bridge bot, the same as `/matrix link`.
`/matrix status` shows the bridge state of the current channel.
`/matrix list` shows every bridged channel in the team.
